**Taste Skill** (`tasteskill 2.5.1`) is an Agent Skill that makes coding agents build professional company websites at the `figma.com` and `x.ai` level instead of assembling a generic landing page. Every build uses plain copy, one design system, one section per screen, equal left and right edges, real photographs (licensed stand-ins when the client has none), real brand icons and real product UI, a hero entrance and one or two dealt moments on every page, quiet micro-interactions, and shader effects and scroll scenes kept strictly for tech, gaming and software pages, all verified in a real browser by a checker and a finish gate that enforce the rules. Pages built from a single brief in earlier v2 runs:
The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ([credits](examples/v2/CREDITS.md)). Watch the [launch film](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/releases/tag/v2.0.0). ## Install ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend" ``` That installs the skill with the [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) CLI. The skill runs its scripts with **Node 22+** and an installed **Chrome, Edge or Chromium** (set `CHROME_PATH` if it is in a non-standard place). Optional: **ffmpeg** on the PATH, for WebP output and the phone crop of a hero photograph in `photos.mjs`. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Bundled Wikimedia Commons photographs work offline; fetching additional photographs or icons uses network access.
Claude Code plugin Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under `taste-skill:`, so it does not collide with your other skills. ``` /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill /plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill ``` `/plugin update` upgrades it later.
Codex plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill ``` Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skill is loaded.
From a clone, linked instead of copied `./install.sh` symlinks the skill into Claude Code (`--codex` for Codex, `--all-agents` for both), so a `git pull` updates it in place. On Windows (Git Bash) it makes a real link, or a directory junction when symlinks are not allowed, and it reports an older copied folder instead of skipping it silently.
Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See [Moved skills](#moved-skills). ## How 2.5 works Use it by asking your agent to build or redesign a company site; the agent loads the skill, copies `assets/` into the project, starts from `assets/starter.html` and runs the checker before it hands the page over. Every build starts by classifying the client's business (`software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service` or `place`) and planning the page screen by screen before writing markup: 1. **Deal tokens and layout.** `scripts/start.mjs` deals a palette made for the trade and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind (`library/palettes.json`, `library/type.json`), and `assets/layout/deal.mjs` deals a hero layout (`split`, `centred`, `product`, `photo`, `place`, `collage`, `editorial`, `word`, `film`, `statement` or `triptych`). 2. **Start from one system.** `assets/starter.html`, `assets/system.css` and `assets/layout/layout.css` enforce one section per screen at desktop (`1440x900`), equal left and right content edges, a fixed navigation bar and a single-screen closing footer (`footer.closing`). 3. **Show real product UI and real photographs.** Software and tech pages populate lit feature cards (`assets/ui/cards.css`) with rewritten HTML UI fragments (`assets/ui/`) and node-and-line diagrams (`assets/diagrams/`), with real brand and interface SVGs resolved locally by `scripts/icons.mjs`. Place, shop, hospitality and non-technical product pages lead with curated photographs (`scripts/photos.mjs`, `assets/photos/`), typography and flat colour, crediting sources in one expandable footer line with no captions under images. 4. **Keep effects for tech and gaming pages.** Shader grounds (`scripts/effects.mjs`), scroll scenes (`assets/scenes/`) and procedural 3D prints (`assets/objects/`) are dealt only on `software`, `tech` and `gaming` pages within a four-context WebGL cap, with static fallbacks for phones and reduced motion. Every page gets a hero entrance and one or two moments from `scripts/moments.mjs`; cafes, hotels, shops, studios and services get only the photo- and type-led ones, and zero WebGL. 5. **Check in a real browser over HTTP.** `scripts/consistency.mjs`, `assets/layout/check.mjs`, `scripts/perf.mjs` and `scripts/shoot.mjs` render the built page in headless Chrome across `1440`, `1024`, `768` and `390`, catching empty visuals, broken shaders, contrast drops, misaligned columns, section-height drift, placeholder text, invented street numbers and slow-network image gaps before the build ships. `scripts/gate.mjs` then holds the finish until no fixable FAIL is left, three rounds at most. Details of what changed from `2.1.x` are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ## The tools Everything is a plain Node 22+ script in the skill folder; none installs anything. | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `scripts/start.mjs` | Deals a palette and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind and prints the `` links and `:root` tokens. | | `assets/layout/deal.mjs` | Deals one of eleven tested hero layouts; `assets/layout/check.mjs` checks it with long-headline stress tests. | | `scripts/photos.mjs` | Deals vetted photographs by trade, enforces image weight and writes the one footer credit line. | | `scripts/icons.mjs` | Resolves real brand and interface icons into local SVG files. | | `scripts/effects.mjs`, `scripts/moments.mjs` | Deal shader grounds for tech, gaming and software pages, and the moments for every kind. | | `scripts/gate.mjs`, `scripts/copy-lint.mjs` | The finish gate (also a Stop hook) and the copy linter it runs. | | `scripts/consistency.mjs` | The checker: renders the page in headless Chrome over HTTP at `1440`, `1024`, `820`, `768` and `390` and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per rule. | | `scripts/perf.mjs`, `scripts/shoot.mjs` | Page weight and speed, and full-page and per-section screenshots. | First run, from the project folder (a deal also arms the finish gate there): `node scripts/start.mjs deal --page software` (kinds: `software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service`, `place`). Check a built page with `node scripts/consistency.mjs --page `. ## Moved skills This repo holds one skill, `design-taste-frontend`. The others moved to repos of their own and kept their install names: | Install name | Where it lives now | | --- | --- | | `high-end-visual-design`, `minimalist-ui`, `industrial-brutalist-ui`, `gpt-taste`, `stitch-design-taste`, `design-taste-frontend-v1`, `design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental` | **[Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics)** | | `imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, `brandkit`, `image-to-code` | **[Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills)** | | `redesign-existing-projects` | Part of `design-taste-frontend`, which audits an existing page in a real browser before changing anything | | `full-output-enforcement` | Removed. For the same problem, see **[Leonxlnx/unlazy](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/unlazy)** | Install a moved skill from its new repo under the same name: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics --skill "high-end-visual-design" ``` ## Common Questions **What does the skill need?** Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium; ffmpeg is optional (WebP photographs and the phone crop of a hero photograph). It installs nothing and uses no API keys. Bundled Commons photographs are stored locally; network access is used only when downloading additional photographs, Google Fonts or brand icons. **Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?** From the skill's vetted photograph library (`assets/photos/photos.json`, including bundled Wikimedia Commons WebP sets and Unsplash photographs) dealt by `scripts/photos.mjs`. Library frames are used for trade and material details (or marked explicitly as draft stand-ins when the client has no photographs yet), never passed off as the client's own room, staff or product, and credited in one expandable footer line (`photos.mjs credits`). **Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?** An empty folder gets a static page from `assets/starter.html`. An existing React, Vue, Svelte, Astro or Tailwind project is built in its own stack, with the kit served from its public folder; a Next.js brief is built as a static export. The browser checks run on the served or built page. **When does a page get shaders or scroll effects?** Shaders only on `software`, `tech` (technical hardware) and `gaming` pages, and always within a four-context WebGL budget with static phone and reduced-motion fallbacks. Places, shops, cafes, hotels, studios, services and everyday physical products stay calm: photographs, sharp typography and flat colour, with a hero entrance and one or two photo- or type-led moments in their own sections. ## Support the project If Taste Skill helps you, consider sponsoring: [Sponsor on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/Leonxlnx) ### Open Source Supporters
